I went through this a couple years back in a similar climate....

Amana is considered 2nd tier (lower grade). There are only 2 grades/tiers from what I could find, and the main difference is materials cost (thinner gauge sheetmetal, cheaper components).

But don't worry ovremuch about unit quality as the quality of installation FAR outweighs what unit is installed. Meaning that you have the Cheapest unit installed by a top notch tech and it'll generally provide you a better experience than the most expensive unit installed by a so-so tech. I found a large number of techs who installed the cheaper units on their own properties and were perfectly happy to do so. Most still cautioned that they didn't always offer those units to clients (based on impression of how much headache the client would cause if something did go wrong).

Last thing, technology has changed in the last decade. Units today use a larger diameter duct with lower pressure, but more volume, and don't play well with older systems that have smaller ducts. The return is the Most important part of this. I had 10" ducts through-out and they swapped the ~6 feet of return to either 14" so as to put less strain on the fan motor.

Generally speaking, it's better to Undersize a unit than to Oversize. You don't want to get into a unit that short cycles as it won't have time to strip the moisture plus it's a huge energy hog to start the system frequently. Running longer is sometimes Cheaper, and generally better for cooling.... obviously, if it's not keeping up with the temp increases then there's an issue. I've got a 2.5ton on my 2,200sq/ft 1930's built (no insulation) house and it has no issues getting the job done. The one I replaced was on a 1970's (pretty well insulated) 1,500sq/ft and was a 2ton ~ looking at NOAA mean temps for houston vs my home, we're a whopping 2~3 degrees apart all year but our humidity is just a little lower (60% ave vs 70% for Houston, again NOAA data).

Best advice, get Multiples of opinions. Discard any where they don't come out to inspect what you have. Give weight to those who have national certifications, and further weight to anyone who does a Load Calculation (often called a ManualJ). Above all, do WAY more research... I spent a week reading and educating myself, this was after my HVAC failed mind you (thankfully in the spring).
Amana is a good brand, but I would get a second opinion.
